properties.areaDesc: Central Mountains; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Upper Sevier River Valleys; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 11:29AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Central
Mountains, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of southern Utah
beginning Wednesday morning, and continuing through Thursday.
Local rainfall totals in excess of 3 inches are expected through
Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

People in the backcountry should ensure they have alternative routes
available in case their primary route becomes impassable.

waterways.

properties.areaDesc: St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 10:03AM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of the northern U.S. Virgin
Islands.

* WHEN...From this evening through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM AST THIS EVENING THROUGH WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 10:03AM AST until October 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Advisory the most vulnerable areas for
high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Barrio
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For High Rip Current Risk,
the most vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and
north- facing beaches. For the High Rip Current Risk, the most
vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and north-facing
beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory remains until 6 PM AST this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk remains through
wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...For the High Surf Advisory, high waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks. Rough
surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will result
in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous swimming
conditions. For the High Rip Current Risk, rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water,
where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 20 at 9:54AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeasterly winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several inches of
water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge
marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and
Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged.
Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp,
docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the
sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: East Carteret
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 20 at 9:46AM EDT until October 20 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents, large
breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...East Carteret County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT Wednesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
is expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some
roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience
shallow flooding. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous
shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the
bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 20 at 9:46AM EDT until October 21 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 6 to 9 feet in the surf zone. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents, large
breaking waves expected, and strong longshore currents in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT
Wednesday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT
this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
is expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be
inundated, especially around high tide. There is a possibility

life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or
surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This is a long duration event with
uncertainty on when conditions will improve. Significant ocean
overwash impacts are expected at vulnerable oceanside areas
through multiple high tide cycles into mid week. Minor
soundside water level rises will also be possible.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 20 at 4:24AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 5 to 11
inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heaviest snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon.
West and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops
quickly. Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting
closer to 2 to 4 inches or less.
properties.instruction:

clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

to the Alcan Border.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Northwest wind gusts may be as high as 35 mph
Tuesday morning through early Wednesday morning.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 7
inches.

* WHERE...Fairbanks, Fox, Chatanika, Ester and Nenena.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall rates will intensify through Tuesday,
with heavier snow expected by late Tuesday morning. There is high
uncertainty in the exact location of this heavier snow area, as a
band looks likely to set up immediately east of the area. This
detail will be crucial in determining which spots get 6 inches or
more versus 3 inches or less. A 30 mile change east or west will
result in drastic differences. If the area of heavier snow shifts
slightly west, heavy snow becomes more likely over the area, and
some areas like North Pole could see greater totals of 7 or even 8
inches. If the area of heavier snow shifts slightly east, heavy
snow becomes less likely over the area.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:
A strong storm system is moving into the northern half of the Alaska
Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast this morning and will
continue through today. Total rain accumulation are expected to be
between 1.5-3.5 inches, with the heaviest rain late Tuesday morning
into Tuesday afternoon. Wet snow is possibly on the Klondike Highway
near White Pass up to 3 inches through tonight, though warm surface
temperatures may hinder these snow totals.

properties.areaDesc: Thompson Pass
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 20 at 2:48AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Additional snow accumulations between 10 and
16 inches, mainly near the top of the pass.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration snowfall event will continue
through tonight. Temperatures at of slightly above freezing will
allow snow to change to rain at times for lower elevations of the
pass. At the top of the pass, snow will be more prolonged but may
also briefly mix with rain at times.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

inches, highest amounts near the mountains.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of Anchorage and the Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Visibilities as low as one half mile possible, including
during the morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will intensify during the overnight hours

properties.areaDesc: Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 2:44AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river, currently over the Yakutat area, is expected
to continue through today. Multiple periods of heavy rain are
expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf Coast,
including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican,
Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated gusty winds are expected alongside this
heavier rainfall, with the strongest winds from the southwest
expected late this morning into this afternoon. Prolonged periods of
moderate to heavy rain will produce significant river rises with the
potential for at least minor flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding
of water in low-lying areas is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast and Northeast Gulf
Coast. This includes the cities of Elfin Cove And Pelican.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Elfin Cove and Pelican area through this
evening range between 3-4 inches, with greater than 6 inches
possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. Coinciding with high
rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches per hour, elevated wind
gusts greater than 40 mph are expected at elevations greater than
500 ft.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
Low relative humidity is forecasted again today. Relative
humidity will fall below 25 percent for much of the afternoon,
especially for northeast Georgia. Given the dry vegetation,
outdoor fires will be able to spread quickly once started,
increasing the danger of wildfires.

Please refer to your local burn permitting authorities on whether
you can burn today. If you do burn, use extreme caution since
fires can quickly get out of hand under these conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Ocean; Atlantic; Cape May; Atlantic Coastal Cape May; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean; Southeastern Burlington
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 20 at 5:07AM EDT until October 20 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May, Atlantic Coastal Cape May,
Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to 9 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional elevated high tide cycles
beyond Tuesday evening are expected with additional coastal
flood hazards likely being needed.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 20 at 1:59AM PDT until October 20 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves. Surf of 3 to 5
feet with local sets to 6 feet. Highest surf on south and
southwest facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
coastal areas.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Areas of hazardous swimming conditions. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash
people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion may occur across
south- facing beaches.
properties.instruction:
A beach hazards statement is issued when threats such as strong
rip currents...elevated surf heights...minor tidal overflow...or
lightning are possible at local beaches. Obey posted warning
signs and flags and talk to a lifeguard before swimming. Use
caution when in or near the water and always swim near a
lifeguard.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 20 at 2:18AM EDT until October 21 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 9 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM EDT Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 19 at 6:51PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
A moderate storm system will impact our coastal waters Wednesday
through Thursday. Activity is likely to be most hazardous for
the waters south and east of Point Conception with peak timing
expected Wednesday afternoon through Thursday morning.

Any thunderstorm that forms will be capable of producing locally
gale force winds and rough seas, dangerous lightning, heavy
rainfall with reduced visibility, and waterspouts..

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 19 at 12:31PM PDT until October 23 at 3:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches especially along the Malibu
Coast and in the Long Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
